_comment: The Refusals page (site/build.py `refusals_page`): what the checker refuses, in plain words, grouped by what a player writes. Each card names a construct (`title`), shows a refused line (`refused`, SystemVerilog unless `lang` says `lean`) and what to write instead (`instead`, code in the same language, or `instead_text`, Markdown inline), and lists the refusal register's rows it stands for (`rows`: ids of docs/sv-refusals.json at the pinned library revision, svGolf's and the language tier's). The rows are shown behind the card's fold, with the register's own reason, state and codes. `more`: the register's svGolf rows a group covers without a card, shown in the group's fold. The build fails when a row named here is not in the register, when an svGolf row of the register (not an aggregate) is on no card and in no group's `more`, or on two, so the page cannot drift from the register: a lifted refusal leaves the register and the page with it. Visible text is plain words: no codes, paths or plan words outside a fold (tests/site).
lead: The checker refuses a design or a proof when the proof and the score could be about different circuits, or when the evidence could be forged. Beyond these refusals and the task's banned operators, write any SystemVerilog the language tier loads. Each card shows a refused line and what to write instead; its details give the full reason.

groups.title: One text for the proof and the score
groups.lead: The proof reads your design through slang, the score through Yosys. Whatever the two would read differently is refused before either runs. Comments are fine: the checker strips them.

cards.title: Macros and conditional compilation
cards.instead:
localparam int W = 4;
if (W > 2) begin : wide
  ...   // a generate if
end

cards.title: Attributes and synthesis comments
cards.refused:
(* keep *) wire t = a & b;
// synopsys translate_off
cards.instead: wire t = a & b;   // a comment
cards.note: A comment that merely names `full_case` or `translate_off` is refused too.

cards.title: unique and priority
cards.refused: unique case (sel) ... endcase
cards.instead:
case (sel)
  ...
  default: y = '0;
endcase
cards.note: Yosys reads the qualifier as a don't-care; the proof runs the first matching arm.

cards.title: Characters outside ASCII
cards.refused: string s = "héllo";
cards.instead_text: Plain ASCII outside comments; anything inside a comment is fine.

cards.title: Anything that reaches the checker's machine
cards.refused:
initial $readmemh("table.hex", mem);
initial $system("id");
cards.instead:
always_comb case (a)
  8'h00: y = 8'h63;
  ...
endcase
cards.note: Files, programs, the environment, wave dumps and DPI are all refused: the checker runs your text on its own machine.

groups.title: No unknown values
groups.lead: The proof computes with x and z as a simulator does; Yosys treats them as don't-cares. So every way an unknown value can arise is refused, at every parameter value the checker tries.

cards.title: x and z in literals
cards.refused: assign y = sel ? a : 'x;
cards.instead: assign y = sel ? a : '0;
cards.note: A `casez` item may use `?` and `z` as wildcards.

cards.title: A constant with unknown bits
cards.refused: localparam logic [3:0] K = 4'd1 / 4'd0;
cards.instead_text: A constant every bit of which is known, and constant selects inside the declared range.

cards.title: An index that can leave the range
cards.refused:
logic [W-1:0] m [4];
assign y = m[i];   // i: 3 bits, 0 to 7
cards.instead: assign y = m[i[1:0]];   // 0 to 3

cards.title: A net nothing drives
cards.refused:
logic u;
assign y = u ? a : b;
cards.instead_text: Drive every net, and every output on every path.

cards.title: Two drivers, loops and latches
cards.note: One driver per net, and no combinational loop, even one that settles.

groups.title: Banned operators
groups.lead: A task bans the run-time operator that is the task, with whatever Yosys builds into the same cells. Arithmetic on parameters and generate indices stays allowed. Each task page lists its banned operators.

cards.title: The operator that is the task
cards.refused: assign {cout, s} = a + b + cin;   // in add
cards.note: add, mul, clmul and the tutorial ban run-time `+ - *`, also in disguise: `+=`, `-a`, `$countones`, a run-time index `a[j + 1]`.

cards.title: Division, remainder and power, in every task
cards.refused: assign q = a / b;
cards.instead_text: Build the quotient from steps of subtraction and comparison, as the fdivp reference does. A zero divisor would make an unknown value from known inputs.

cards.title: Ordering comparisons where + and - are banned
cards.refused: assign cout = a > ~b;
cards.instead_text: `==` and `!=` stay allowed; build `<` from gates. Yosys builds a run-time `a < b` as its own adder.

groups.title: What the language tier cannot load yet
groups.lead: Your proof is about the design as Proglib's extractor and loader read it, and the score about what the pinned Yosys reads. These common constructs fail at one of the two for now.

cards.title: Procedural for loops
cards.note: The loop counter as an index is refused, because the index check does not know loop bounds; only one simple loop header is accepted at all.

cards.title: What the pinned Yosys cannot read
cards.note: Yosys 0.53 also cannot read `inside` or an unpacked constant array.

cards.title: Constant tables as arrays
Casts to a parameter width, and $signed into a wider value
cards.refused:
assign y = N'(a & b);
assign w = $signed(a);  // w wider than a
cards.instead:
assign w = {a[N-1], a};  // sign-extend
assign t = 8'(a);        // fixed width

cards.title: Gate primitives
cards.refused: and g1(y, a, b);
cards.instead: assign y = a & b;

cards.title: Extra parameters on the top module
cards.refused:
module band #(parameter int N = 4,
              parameter int M = 2) (...);
cards.instead:
module band #(parameter int N = 4) (...);
  localparam int M = 2;
cards.note: The scoring flow sets the task's parameters by name, so the top declares exactly those, none narrower than `int`.

groups.title: The statement: ports, clocks and every size
groups.lead: The trusted statement fixes the ports and what the design computes, at every parameter value in the task's range. A design that breaks it has no proof.

cards.title: Ports other than the task's
cards.refused:
input logic ci,   // the task's is cin
input logic en,   // an extra input
cards.instead_text: The task page's ports, exactly: names, order and widths.

cards.title: A clocked process in a combinational task
cards.refused:
always_ff @(posedge clk)   // in add
  s <= a ^ b;
cards.instead: assign s = a ^ b;
cards.note: Registers belong to the clocked tasks.

cards.title: A proof for one size only
cards.refused: -- a proof that holds at N = 16 only
cards.instead:
-- a proof for every N in the task's range,
-- for example by induction on the bit index

groups.title: Clocked tasks
groups.lead: matmul, sorter and the arbiter are clocked. A clocked design runs on one clock edge and must be right from any power-up state, so these are refused there.

cards.title: An asynchronous reset or a second clock
cards.refused: always_ff @(posedge clk or posedge rst)

cards.title: Initial values, blocking writes and delays
cards.refused:
logic [3:0] cnt = '0;
always_ff @(posedge clk) q = d;
cards.instead:
logic [3:0] cnt;   // reset it instead
always_ff @(posedge clk) q <= d;

cards.title: A register nothing loads
cards.refused:
always_ff @(posedge clk) u <= u;
assign sel = !u;
cards.note: The pinned flow removes such a register and reads an arbitrary value at each use.

cards.title: An index that can leave the vector
cards.refused:
always_ff @(posedge clk)
  q <= v[i];       // v: 8 bits, i: 4
cards.instead:
always_ff @(posedge clk)
  q <= v[i[2:0]];

cards.title: An output that reads an input directly
cards.refused: assign out_valid = ov_q & ~rst;
cards.instead: assign out_valid = ov_q;   // a register
cards.note: In the transaction and stream tasks no output may read an input combinationally, the reset included; clear the register in the reset branch instead.

groups.title: The proof file
groups.lead: The kernel must accept your theorem from the task's allowed axioms alone, in one file that imports only what the checker builds.

cards.title: Anything the kernel does not check
cards.refused:
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by
  native_decide     -- or sorry
axiom cheat : Submission.Goal
cards.instead:
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by
  -- tactics the kernel checks:
  -- decide +kernel, omega, simp, ...
cards.note: `bv_decide` is not supported: it runs an external solver.

cards.title: Imports the checker does not build
cards.refused:
import MyHelpers
import Lake
cards.instead:
import Submission.Design
import SvGolf.Comb
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
cards.note: One file. Mathlib and its packages are allowed.

cards.title: The latency line
cards.refused:
-- svgolf-latency: 3
-- svgolf-latency: 4
cards.instead: -- svgolf-latency: 3
cards.note: Transaction and stream tasks only: exactly one such line, the number of cycles.

groups.title: After synthesis
groups.lead: The checker synthesizes the design with the pinned flow, simulates the proof's semantics against the netlist and weighs the netlist on the sky130 cells. A refusal here means the tools disagree: report it, it is a bug in one of them.

groups.title: For task authors
groups.lead: Mistakes in a task definition fail loudly, so that a typo cannot change the tests or the banned operators.
